roi.heading: Microsoft 365 license waste calculator
roi.intro: Put in your paid seat count, your monthly cost per seat and a waste share you consider plausible, and see what that assumption costs per month and per year. The estimate runs entirely in your browser, and a free read-only scan replaces it with your tenant's real number.

drivers.heading: What typically drives license waste
drivers.intro: The waste share you pick above is an assumption, but the mechanisms behind it are concrete. These are the patterns LicenseMeter's detection rules look for in real tenants:

items.title: Offboarding leaks
items.body: An account gets disabled in Entra ID, but its licenses stay assigned. The seat keeps billing every month until someone notices. This is the classic leak: leavers accumulate quietly, one or two per departure.

items.title: Seats that never started
items.body: Licenses assigned ahead of onboarding, for a project that fizzled, or by an over-broad group rule. The user never signs in and never touches a workload, yet the seat is paid from day one.

items.title: Seats that went quiet
items.body: People change roles, tools change, and a licensed account stops signing in to Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint or Teams. Without a last-activity check across those workloads, the seat looks fine in the admin center.

items.title: Shelfware, overlaps and add-ons
items.body: Purchased seats that were never assigned to anyone, suites paid alongside standalone plans that duplicate them, Copilot add-ons nobody uses, and paid licenses sitting on guest accounts. None of this shows up in a headcount comparison.

how.heading: How the calculator works
how.body: Seats times monthly cost per seat times your assumed waste share: no more, no less. The math runs in integer cents, the annual figure is twelve times the monthly one. LicenseMeter is free regardless of seat count. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

detection.heading: From assumption to detection
detection.intro: A scan replaces the slider with findings: LicenseMeter joins directory data, license assignments, sign-in activity and usage reports read-only, then prices every wasted seat from an editable price book prefilled with list-price estimates, because there is no Microsoft API for your negotiated prices.
detection.stats: The sample tenant of {users} people shows
detection.suffix: a month across {findingsCount} findings, each with the account, the rule and the monthly cost attached.
detection.note: Every finding exports to CSV for finance, and IT gets a generated PowerShell remediation script to review and run. LicenseMeter itself never writes to your tenant.

final.heading: Stop estimating. See your number.
final.body: Connect read-only and the free scan replaces every assumption on this page with real tenant data, priced per seat and per month.
final.note: Free scans and continuous monitoring. No credit card, read-only access.
